gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: cough and cold for 5 days. Generated facts hpi-001 and cc-001 both describe cough/cold symptoms for ~5 days, matching duration and nature of complaint.
Gold: cough is dry, no sputum or blood. Generated facts hpi-002 and hpi-003 state the cough is dry, hacking, without phlegm/sputum or blood, capturing all elements.
Gold: patient denies wheezing. Generated hpi-005 (no wheezing) and pe-004 (no wheeze) both include this denial.
Gold: patient denies breathlessness. Generated hpi-005 states no shortness of breath and plan-004/fu-001 reference SOB as a warning, which aligns with initial denial.
Gold: patient reports a headache. Generated hpi-004 and ros-001 both list headaches among current symptoms.
Gold: patient reports no swollen neck glands. Generated ros-002 notes no neck gland swelling and pe-003 notes no palpable lymphadenopathy, which is equivalent.
Gold: diabetes for 5–6 years. Generated pmh-001 states diabetes mellitus for 5–6 years, matching exactly.
Gold: patient has hypertension. Generated pmh-002 confirms hypertension.
Gold: patient is taking metformin. Generated med-001, asm-006, plan-005, plan-010 all confirm ongoing metformin use.
Gold: patient is taking lisinopril. Generated med-002, asm-008, plan-005, plan-010 confirm lisinopril use.
Gold: patient has used paracetamol for symptoms. Generated med-003 and plan-002 state paracetamol used/recommended for symptom relief in current illness.
Gold: redness at back of throat on video assessment. Generated pe-002 documents mild redness at the back of the throat, which aligns with this finding.
Gold: tonsils not enlarged. Generated pe-002: no enlarged tonsils, directly matching.

Gold: BP and blood sugar normal today. Generated notes do not explicitly state that today’s sugar and BP are normal; asm-008 mentions recent BP reportedly normal and asm-006 says BG monitoring without issues, but not specifically today. Therefore this precise fact is not captured.

Gold: diagnosis upper respiratory tract infection. Generated asm-001 and asm-002 specify acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold), consistent with and slightly more specific than the gold diagnosis.
Gold: advised to use Night Nurse and Day Nurse preparations. Generated plan-001 and plan-008 both advise use of Night Nurse and Day Nurse for symptomatic relief.

Gold: call back if breathlessness, wheezing, or cough >3 weeks. Generated plan-003, plan-004, and fu-001 collectively advise contact/return if symptoms worsen, SOB/wheezing/respiratory distress develop, or symptoms persist beyond three weeks.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Chief complaint repeats cough and cold for ~5 days; matches the gold HPI duration and symptoms.
Five-day history of coughing and cold-type symptoms aligns with gold statement of cough and cold for 5 days; runny nose is an added detail but consistent.
Describes dry cough without phlegm, consistent with gold dry cough with no sputum.
States cough not associated with blood, matching gold ‘no blood’ in the cough.
Muscle aches, chills, and general cold symptoms are not mentioned in the gold facts; headache is supported by gold but the other symptoms are additional.
No shortness of breath and no wheezing match gold denials of breathlessness and wheeze; rattling sounds in chest are an added negative detail not present in gold.
Diabetes mellitus for 5–6 years matches gold diabetes since 5–6 years.
Hypertension matches gold past medical history of high blood pressure.
Metformin use supported by gold; note about missing dose/route/frequency is neutral metadata.
Lisinopril use supported by gold; missing dosing details are neutral additions.
Use of paracetamol for current symptoms is consistent with gold ‘used paracetamol.’
Alert and not in acute distress is not described anywhere in the gold facts.
Mild redness at back of throat and no enlarged tonsils matches gold redness at back of throat and no tonsillar enlargement.
No palpable lymphadenopathy in the neck supports gold ‘no swollen glands around neck felt.’
No wheeze or abnormal respiratory sounds per history is consistent with gold patient denies wheezing; absent abnormal sounds are additional but not contradictory.
Dry cough and headache are supported by gold, but runny nose, muscle aches, and chills are not mentioned in gold, so overall this is an addition.
No blood in sputum matches gold no blood; also aligns with no shortness of breath (hpi-004), no wheezing (hpi-003), and no neck gland swelling (hpi-006).
Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) is a more specific description of the gold ‘upper respiratory tract infection’ but not contradictory.

States presentation consistent with viral URI and no evidence of bacterial infection or lower respiratory involvement; the viral vs. bacterial distinction and lower tract comment are not present in gold.
Differential diagnosis of bacterial pharyngitis and reasoning based on tonsils/lymphadenopathy is not mentioned in gold facts.
Differential of bronchitis and rationale (no wheezing or sputum) is not in gold facts.
Gold notes diabetes but does not categorize it as ‘controlled’; this controlled status is additional clinical interpretation.
Gold confirms metformin use but does not mention blood glucose monitoring or that there are no issues; those details are additional.
Gold notes hypertension but does not label it ‘controlled’; control status is additional.
Gold does not specify recent BP results; ‘recent BP reportedly normal’ is additional, and not clearly the same as ‘normal today.’
Use of Night Nurse and Day Nurse for symptomatic management matches gold advice; statement of safety with current meds is additional but not conflicting.
Recommending paracetamol for pain/fever is consistent with gold ‘used paracetamol for symptoms’; direction of recommendation vs. reported use is compatible.
Monitoring for symptoms not resolving after 3 weeks aligns with gold instruction to call back if cough >3 weeks.
Advising to seek care if shortness of breath or wheezing develops matches gold call-back for breathlessness or wheezing; ‘increased severity of symptoms’ is an added but consistent caution.
Continuing metformin and lisinopril is not explicitly stated in gold; gold only lists them as active meds.
Advice to continue home glucose/BP monitoring is not mentioned in gold facts.
Explicit statement of no regimen changes for diabetes and hypertension is not found in gold facts.
Instruction to use Night Nurse and Day Nurse as needed for symptom relief matches gold advice to use night and day nurse.
General instruction to monitor for signs of progression or complications is broader and not specifically described in the gold follow-up statement.
Maintaining usual medication and home monitoring routines is not present in the gold facts.
Telemedicine management and no prescription needed are not mentioned in gold facts.

Advised to return/contact if symptoms worsen, respiratory distress develops, or persist beyond 3 weeks is conceptually aligned with gold call-back for worsening symptoms including breathlessness/wheezing or cough beyond 3 weeks.
